positives.query: A service starts background work with asyncio and never keeps the object that comes back; a reviewer says the work may vanish mid-run. Should I call that a confirmed bug?
Our API handler kicks off a synchronous job per request. Someone proposes a raw thread per call for throughput. Is the built-in route already capped, and how would I raise the cap?
An endpoint returns nested Pydantic models with exclude-unset switched on, and a client reports that inner keys which have defaults are missing from the JSON.
A test counts the routes on a freshly built FastAPI app to prove only my endpoints exist, but the count is higher than expected, and the routes of a sub-router I mounted seem absent from the table.
A HEAD request to my FastAPI GET endpoint gets a 405 when another route matches the same path, while the identical setup on plain Starlette answers it.
My single-page-app static mount overrides error handling to return index.html on a missing file, but a missing path still gets the built-in 404 page when the directory ships one.
I listed two different 422 payloads for one route in the OpenAPI responses mapping, but only one of them appears in the generated schema.
I registered handlers for a base exception and for its subclass; my error-body test passes although the custom handler never ran, and a later registration silently replaced an earlier one.
A middleware allows admin endpoints only when the caller address is loopback; behind a reverse proxy any client can look local. Why does that check not hold?
My request model requires a name of minimum length one, yet a name made only of spaces was accepted and stored.
I wrapped a urlopen call with a timeout in an except for the URL error class and a slow server still crashed my code with an uncaught error.
A numeric validator parses user JSON and my finiteness check never fires: a bare NaN token got through and broke later comparisons.
My client pointed at the local model server without the version path segment received a success status, but the body was an error message, and my retry logic counted it as good.
Code that parses a model's JSON answer began failing on every reply after switching model families; the replies look valid when printed but are wrapped in triple-backtick blocks.
My test sets an environment variable with monkeypatch to change a config constant, but the code still sees the old value, and only when the whole suite runs, not when the file runs alone.
A test expecting a validation error with a given exception type passes, yet when I break the very check it targets the test still passes.
A completeness test over results recorded by sibling tests breaks on a subset run; I skipped it on the keyword filter but a run selecting by node id still fails it.
After a scripted edit removed a test function, a neighbouring test suddenly runs with odd parameters and fails with argument errors.
Patching a name in another module with monkeypatch works for one function that imports it inside its body but has no effect on another function where the same name is a default argument value.
Adding an import of module B's name into module A, where B already imports from A, fails in both import orders even though the names are unrelated; moving it to class level did not help.

My lifespan starts a polling task and never cancels it at shutdown, yet a test using the test client says the task was cancelled once the context-manager block closes, hiding the missing cancellation.
To check what an actual HTTP caller would get on an unhandled server error I asserted a 500 status, but the test itself dies with the original exception.
Importing the Starlette test client prints a deprecation warning telling me to install a different HTTP package, and our CI treats warnings as errors.
I patch an object stored on the application state in a fixture before any request and get an AttributeError saying the state has no such attribute.

A test already holds an entered test client with patches applied through it and I need the 500 behaviour for one assertion; building a second client wrapping the same application object lost my patches.
A worker pool's submit is called while holding our own lock and I worry the interpreter hangs forever at exit; how long does exit actually block?
A per-caller busy flag is reset right after handing work to a thread pool, and intermittently the end state is wrong because the worker already finished.
I want to prove a function finishes inside a deadline it computes itself; my test timed the call and asserted afterwards, but when the function hangs CI just kills the job naming no test.
I changed a one-character constant in a module and re-ran immediately; Python still prints the old value although the file clearly changed, and the don't-write-bytecode variable did not fix it.
Code under test calls input() to ask for confirmation; in the test run it throws an OSError about reading from stdin instead of waiting.
I want a test asserting that my fake implements every method a Protocol declares, without keeping a separate hard-coded list of names.
I ran the Python linter over a list of changed files that included a markdown changelog and got a flood of syntax errors on ordinary sentences.
I ran the code formatter on one file to clear two long-line warnings and my diff now touches hundreds of unrelated lines.
Several slow callbacks queued after one response are delayed by the first slow one, even though the thread pool has idle workers.
My except ladder for ValueError around a call that opens a URL with a bad port did not catch the failure; it surfaced as an unclassified exception type.
I told pytest to skip one specific test by passing its absolute path to the deselect option, and it still ran, with no warning.
An MCP tool parameter has a maximum length; a client sending too long a value gets a tool result flagged as an error, not a protocol error, and I cannot find the bound in the advertised schema.
My script reads the pass and fail counts from the last line of the doubly-quiet pytest output, and a failing run reports zero failures.
To avoid stale compiled files I pointed the bytecode cache location at an empty temp folder and it worked, but later ordinary runs still show stale code. What did that fix leave behind?
A test spawns a subprocess with no stdin argument and prints where its standard input points; it shows the null device, not the pipe my shell gave me, so my stdin-inheritance test proves nothing.
After sending a termination signal to a process group and waiting on the leader, a child that ignores the signal survives and my file lock stays held, blocking the next acquirer.
My mutation-testing copy of the repo is ignored when tests are executed via the bare pytest command, which imports the original tree, though python -m pytest picks up the copy.

negatives.query: One coroutine in an asyncio.gather call raised, but its siblings keep running in the background. How do I make them cancel when the first one fails?
In tests I need to replace the authentication dependency of a FastAPI route with a fake user, and the override seems ignored for a sub-dependency.
An async SQLAlchemy session is not closed on an error path and under load the connection pool runs dry with timeouts.
A session-scoped pytest fixture seems to run once per worker under xdist, and my shared temporary database is populated several times.
uvicorn --reload does not pick up edits when the source is a bind-mounted Docker volume.
A pydantic v2 model should accept one field name on input but emit another on output; which setting does that?
mypy reports an Optional as still possibly None after I narrowed it inside a walrus condition.
How should I structure a React Server Components data-fetching boundary to avoid request waterfalls in a Next.js app?
How do I configure a Kubernetes readiness probe for a FastAPI container whose startup depends on a slow database connection?
How can I make a multi-stage Dockerfile reuse the dependency layer when only application code changed?
A git rebase stops with conflicts in a lockfile; what is the safe way to resolve it and continue?
A CSS grid layout overflows its container on narrow phones even though the columns use fr units.
A pandas groupby-apply over a few million rows is slow; what is the idiomatic faster form?
A Postgres table's index keeps growing after heavy updates; how do I reclaim the space without downtime?
